reviews.author: Manuel São Bento
reviews.content:
I headed into this 2025 reimagining of ANACONDA - not a remake! - with a mix of cautious optimism and a heavy dose of nostalgia for the 1997 original. Having followed Tom Gormican's knack for meta-humor, I was curious to see if he could successfully transplant that self-aware energy into a creature feature. What I found was a film that thrives when it leans into its own absurdity, particularly through a movie-within-a-movie satire that mirrors the chaotic, often delusional passion of indie filmmaking. The central dynamic between Paul Rudd and Jack Black is the undeniable heartbeat of the experience; their natural chemistry makes the midlife-crisis subtext feel surprisingly grounded amidst the jungle mayhem. However, the true scene-stealer is Selton Mello, who delivers a hilariously eccentric performance that perfectly captures the film's comedic aspirations. It's a journey that feels like a heartfelt tribute to the struggle of creation, even when the actual "creation" is a B-movie disaster.

Despite these highs, the film frequently trips over its own tonal inconsistencies, struggling to bridge the gap between sharp Hollywood satire and a genuine horror-thriller. This imbalance is most apparent in the lackluster VFX; the titular snake often feels weightless and digital, lacking the physical menace that made the original's animatronics so memorable. My biggest disappointment, however, lies in how the script handles its supporting cast. As someone who has championed Daniela Melchior from the start, seeing her relegated to such an underdeveloped, shallow role was frustrating — she, just like Thandiwe Newton, deserves much more than being mere background noise to the lead duo's antics. Coupled with a redundant subplot involving illegal miners that adds unnecessary bloat, the movie loses its way whenever it drifts from its core comedic premise. 

Ultimately, ANACONDA is a fun, meta-experiment that works best as a character-driven comedy, even if it fails to leave a lasting mark as a creature feature.

Rating: B-

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Perhaps if they’d screened the first version of this story from 1997 followed by the whole of “Quatch” then I might have better appreciated this Sony reboot of the story? Then again, maybe not. Right from the start, we know that there is a giant snake at large and so when recently fired bit-part actor “Griff” (Paul Rudd) suggests to his “Quatch” co-star, wedding video director “Doug” (Jack Black) that he has acquired the rights to remake “Anaconda” - only without Eric Stolz, they leap at the opportunity and set off with pals “Claire” (Thandiwe Newton); “Kenny” (Steve Zahn) and slightly less than ten thousand bucks. Before they even manage to embark on their boat, though, they find themselves caught up in some local gold smuggling shenanigans thanks to “Ana” (Daniela Melchior) and then another - legitimate - film crew sails onto the scene, too. “Ana” turns out to be quite the action-hero and soon there is friction on the boat, “Griff” has gone off in the huff and yep, eventually, our scaly terror begins to make it’s presence felt. When I say scaly, I could mean leather skinned or I could mean a creature that appears to grow and shrink in size depending on the scenario. At some points it’s like “Godzilla”, at others more like “Godzooki” - so it’s more a sort of comedy menace from the cutting room floor of a “Jurassic Park”. Jack Black looks like he is enjoying himself as he traipses through the foliage chewing on regurgitated squirrel but that’s about the standard of the comedy here; there’s not much of it, and by the time we get to the sharp end of the film I was a bit bored. Perhaps the plan was to parody loads of other features from this genre? Rudd and Black work well together, but there simply isn’t enough for them to work with as the storyline dissolves disappointingly. It wasn’t really a plot that needed a second shot, and sadly this rather proves that point but it’s watchable Chrimbo-limbo cinema fodder - just nobody’s finest hour, not even the snake’s.

reviews.author: Enes
reviews.content: It was more fun than scary. Especially the scene at the end where the guy shows off his actions in public as an achievement was great 😂 I liked it and it's definitely worth watching. The acting is fantastic, the effects are good, and the script is entertaining. I think it deserves a 7 out of 10. Thank you for your hard work.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
Technically proficient, creatively dead inside
This is a parody of itself, a low-effort attempt at sincerity and with great acting to gloss it all over. It is not a good movie, although technically proficient and looking lovely, the story just does not carry, despite the heroic effort of the actors involved. If you want a good Anaconda go rewatch the 90s one. Even one or two of the sequels. They were not as pretty, but they had more heart.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A group of middle-aged friends attempting to remake their favorite childhood film in the rainforest must fight for survival against giant snakes, dangerous criminals, and unpredictable nature.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Facing mid-life crises, a group of lifelong friends travels deep into the rainforest to recreate their favorite movie from their youth. However, their lighthearted filmmaking passion project quickly turns into a desperate struggle for survival. Surrounded by natural disasters, lethal giant snakes, and hostile criminals, they are forced to band together in ways they never anticipated.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Feeling stuck in their routine lives and longing for the passion of their youth, a circle of friends decides to confront their mid-life crises with an ambitious adventure. They pack their gear and head deep into the rainforest to shoot a remake of the beloved movie that brought them together years ago. What begins as a nostalgic and comedic filmmaking expedition rapidly devolves into chaotic peril. Unforgiving weather and sudden natural disasters strike their camp, threatening to strand them far from civilization. To make matters worse, they cross paths with a ruthless gang of violent criminals operating in the dense jungle. As if human threats and nature's fury were not enough, massive, deadly snakes begin hunting them through the undergrowth. With their equipment destroyed and their lives on the line, the friends must rely on their ingenuity, humor, and deep-seated bonds to navigate the nightmare. Ultimate survival requires them to step into the roles of the true heroes they always dreamed of becoming.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Driven by a shared desire to reignite their youthful spark amidst mid-life crises, a close-knit group of friends journeys into a remote rainforest to remake their favorite childhood movie. What starts as a humorous, nostalgic passion project morphs into an intense battle for survival when they encounter extreme weather, armed criminals, and terrifying giant snakes. Combining elements of adventure, comedy, horror, and drama, this story explores friendship, resilience, and the wild unpredictability of chasing one's dreams into the deep jungle.

story_structure.climax: In a frantic, high-stakes battle for survival, the friends must pool their limited resources and rely on one another to overcome both lethal apex predators and armed criminals.
story_structure.conflict: The group's lighthearted movie project devolves into true survival as the extreme environment presents unexpected threats, testing their resolve and personal bonds.
story_structure.resolution: With the primary threats defeated, the surviving friends escape the jungle, emerging from the life-threatening ordeal with a newfound appreciation for life and deepened camaraderie.
story_structure.introduction: A group of middle-aged friends dealing with mid-life crises journey into a remote rainforest with the goal of remaking their favorite film from their youth.
story_structure.risingAction: Tensions mount as the friends navigate a gauntlet of compounding dangers, including severe natural disasters, predatory giant snakes, and confrontations with violent criminals.

characters.name: Doug McCallister
characters.description: An unfulfilled wedding videographer who leads his friends into the Amazon to follow his dream of directing, ultimately stepping up to save his friends and face down the ultimate dangers.

characters.name: Ronald "Griff" Griffin Jr.
characters.description: A struggling actor whose selfish lies and ego drive the group into danger, though he eventually redeems himself by fighting alongside his friends.

characters.name: Kenny Trent
characters.description: An eccentric, self-proclaimed 'Buffalo sober' friend whose quirky antics and chaotic energy provide constant humor amidst life-threatening situations.

characters.name: Claire Simons
characters.description: A grounded member of the friend group who manages old romantic tensions with Griff while helping keep the team focused on surviving.

characters.name: Ana Almeida
characters.description: An illegal gold miner who tricks the group under false pretenses and turns violently against them at gunpoint to force them into labor.

characters.name: Carlos Santiago Braga
characters.description: An eccentric snake handler hired by the group who serves as their ill-fated guide into the treacherous jungle.

characters.name: Ice Cube
characters.description: Appearing as himself on location, he equips and advises the stranded group on how to survive and conquer the monstrous threats.
